audit.whatIsWrong: Content-layer prose misgenders Leona with she/her throughout (early/mid/late/whys/spikes/wants).
audit.why: Leona is not in the project's female-champion list for this lane slice, so the pronoun convention defaults to he/him. The full layer already avoids gendered pronouns for Leona (already correct), but champ-data/content/sup/rell.js consistently uses she/her.
audit.corrected: Swap she/her/hers to he/him/his throughout, including object-pronoun cases (let her whiff -> let him whiff, Let her commit -> Let him commit) that a blind find-replace would get wrong.

audit.why: Leona out-engages Rell levels 1-5 with a longer-range dash-root (Zenith Blade, 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s cd) that lands before Rell can walk up and W-slam; Rell only takes over once Magnet Storm (level 6) gives her a teamfight answer to Solar Flare. Content already frames this correctly.

content.spikes already tracks the real power-spike pattern: Leona wins the level-2 engage race, the matchup flips at level 6 when Magnet Storm answers Solar Flare, and Rell out-lasts her front-loaded combo once items are online.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[N].side is the placeholder "Skill" on all 7 rows in the full layer, but content win[] reads ["Leona","Leona","Leona","Leona","Leona","Rell","Rell"] and the packet levelChart independently agrees exactly, with no defect flagged (winRate 51.98%, 3813 games).
audit.why: For rows 0-3 (Levels 1-3, 4-5) and rows 5-6 (first item, 2+ items), win[] and the packet agree and the full layer's own breakdown.mid text ("The lane swings at 6 when your Magnet Storm...") supports the same turn point, so I synced side to match. Row 4 (Level 6) is the one place win[4]="Leona" and the packet chart agree with each other, but content.whys[4] ("At 6 your Magnet Storm flips it — you out-teamfight her single-target ult") and full breakdown.mid both describe Rell taking over exactly at level 6 — a genuine content-layer self-contradiction I cannot resolve from the kit alone (I do not have per-stage win-rate data, only the packet's single levelChart value).
audit.corrected: Sync phases[0..3].side to "Leona" and phases[5..6].side to "Rell" (win[] already correct for these rows, no win[] edit needed). Leave phases[4].side ("Skill") and win[4] ("Leona") untouched — flagged in notes rather than guessed.

edits.before: Leona out-engages you at levels 1-5 — her E dash-root is a longer, faster lock than your walk-up dismount, so if she lands it on your ADC you're stunned before you can W-slam. Respect her E range, hug your ADC, and don't facecheck brush where a Zenith Blade is waiting. Ward defensively and let her whiff a dash before you ever consider counter-engaging.
edits.after: Leona out-engages you at levels 1-5 — his E dash-root is a longer, faster lock than your walk-up dismount, so if he lands it on your ADC you're stunned before you can W-slam. Respect his E range, hug your ADC, and don't facecheck brush where a Zenith Blade is waiting. Ward defensively and let him whiff a dash before you ever consider counter-engaging.

edits.before: Through levels 3-5 Leona keeps the initiation edge with her front-loaded CC chain, so play reactive: bait her E, then punish the cooldown. Your W stun is your counter-engage tool, not your opener here. The lane swings at 6 when your Magnet Storm gives you a teamfight answer her single-target ult lacks.

Your W stun is your counter-engage tool, not your opener here. The lane swings at 6 when your Magnet Storm gives you a teamfight answer his single-target ult lacks.

edits.before: From 6 onward you take over — your R plus W engage out-teamfights her point-and-click Solar Flare, and your sustained CC chain outlasts her burst combo. Let her commit her lockdown, body-block for your carry, then W-stun and Magnet Storm the return fight. On items your aura and zone control dominate the extended fight she can't win.
